'''''Senecio elegans''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[asteraceae|aster family]] known by the common names '''redpurple ragwort''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SEEL|taxon=Senecio elegans|accessdate=9 November 2015}}</ref> '''purple groundsel''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''wild cineraria''' and '''purple ragwort'''.

==Description==
It is an annual herb producing a single, erect, branching stem which grows to a maximum height around 60 centimeters. The leaves have blades up to about 8 centimeters long which are deeply cut or divided into several toothed lobes. The herbage is somewhat hairy and glandular, sticky to the touch. The [[inflorescence]] bears [[Head (botany)|flower head]]s lined with black-tipped [[bract|phyllaries]]. They contain many yellowish disc florets at the center. Each has usually 13 ray florets 1 to 1.5 centimeters long which can be most any shade of red-purple.

==Distribution==
It is endemic to the [[Cape Provinces]] of [[South Africa]], and it is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] for its colorful flowers. It has been known to [[escaped plant|escape cultivation]] and become [[introduced species|naturalized]] in areas of appropriate climate; it can be found growing wild in parts of [[New Zealand]], [[Australia]],<ref name=VRO>{{cite web|title= Purple Groundsel|work=Victorian Resources Online| publisher=Department of Primary Industries (Victoria)|url=http://vro.dpi.vic.gov.au/dpi/vro/vrosite.nsf/pages/sip_purple_groundsel|access-date=2 April 2012}}</ref> the [[Azores]], and on the [[Central Coast of California]]. It favors a [[Mediterranean climate]], often on the coast.
